title: Symmetry and Monotonicity of y = sqrt(|x|)
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Describe the graph of y = sqrt(|x|), identify its symmetry, and specify the intervals where the function is increasing and where it is decreasing.
finalAnswer: \text{Symmetric about the } y\text{-axis; Decreasing on } (-\infty, 0]; \text{ Increasing on } [0, \infty)

steps.title: Establish Even Symmetry
steps.explanation: The natural domain is (-inf, inf), and replacing x with -x leaves sqrt(|x|) unchanged, so the graph is symmetric across the y-axis.
steps.why: The composition of sqrt(u) with the even function u = |x| is an even function.

steps.title: Determine Monotonicity on [0, inf)
steps.explanation: For x >= 0, y = sqrt(x), which is strictly increasing on [0, inf) starting from (0, 0).
steps.why: The principal square root function is strictly increasing on [0, inf).

steps.title: Determine Monotonicity on (-inf, 0]
steps.explanation: For x <= 0, y = sqrt(-x). As x increases toward 0, -x decreases toward 0, so sqrt(-x) decreases to 0. Thus the function decreases on (-inf, 0] and increases on [0, inf).
steps.why: Mirror reflection across the y-axis reverses the direction of monotonicity on (-inf, 0].
